title: Study 17, phase 1: which solution do agents pick, the better one or their own?

features.title: Expiring share links
features.request:
Add expiring share links to notes.js. Everything that is there must keep working.

- `createShareLink(userId, noteId, ttlMs = 86400000)` returns a token: a URL-safe string (letters, digits, `-` and `_`). Only the note's owner may create one; otherwise the same errors as getNote (NotFoundError for an unknown user or note, ForbiddenError for someone else's note). `ttlMs` must be a whole number of milliseconds from 1 to 30 days (2592000000); anything else throws ValidationError.
- `openShareLink(token)` needs no user. It returns `{ id, text, tags }` of the note as it is now. A link stops working when `now >= the time it was created + ttlMs`, when it is revoked, or when its note is deleted. Then, and for any token that is not a live link, it throws NotFoundError, always with the same message, so a caller cannot tell why.
- `revokeShareLink(userId, token)`: only the owner of the note may revoke (ForbiddenError otherwise); a token that is not a link throws NotFoundError.
- Anyone who has a link can read the note, so tokens must be impossible to guess.
- It must stay fast with many links: with 100,000 live links, opening one takes about as long as with ten.

features.title: Import notes from CSV
features.request:
Add `importCsv(userId, csv)` to notes.js. Everything that is there must keep working.

It creates notes for that user from CSV text and returns `{ imported, errors }`: `imported` is how many notes were created, `errors` a list of `{ line, reason }` for the records that were skipped (`line` is the 1-based line number in the input where the record starts, the header being line 1; `reason` a short text).

- The first line is a header. It must have a `text` column; a `tags` column is optional; other columns are ignored, in any order. No `text` column: ValidationError, nothing imported.
- Fields follow RFC 4180: separated by commas; a field may be in double quotes, and then may contain commas, line breaks and doubled quotes (`""` stands for one `"`). Lines end with \n or \r\n. A byte-order mark at the start is ignored. Empty lines are skipped.
- `tags` holds tags separated by `;`, with spaces around each trimmed; empty means no tags. A record whose text or tags createNote would refuse is skipped and reported; the others are still imported.
- Notes are always created for `userId`, whatever the file says.
- Limits: a `csv` that is not a string, or longer than 1,000,000 characters, or with more than 5,000 records, throws ValidationError and imports nothing. An unknown user throws NotFoundError.
- It must stay fast: 5,000 records of a few hundred characters each import in well under a second.

features.title: A per-user write limit
features.request:
Add a per-user limit on writes to notes.js. Everything that is there must keep working.

- Writes are createNote, updateNote and deleteNote. Each user may make at most `writeLimit` writes in any `writeWindowMs`, as a sliding window: a write made at time t counts against the user's later writes until t + writeWindowMs (at t + writeWindowMs it no longer counts). Both are options of the constructor: `new NotesService({ now, writeLimit = 30, writeWindowMs = 60000 })`.
- A write by a user who is at the limit throws `RateLimitError` (export it, like the other errors), whatever else is wrong with the write. The error has a number `retryAfterMs`: the milliseconds until that user's next write would be allowed. A limited write changes nothing.
- Only writes that succeed count. A write that throws (not found, forbidden, invalid or limited) does not count, for anyone.
- Reads (getNote, listNotes) are never limited. One user's writes never affect another user's limit.
- It must stay fast: with writeLimit 100,000, one user's 100,000 writes inside one window take well under a second; and the work per write must not grow with the user's past writes.
